messages.subject: Importing Latex tables
parts:
Hi there,

I am considering writing my Master's thesis in markdown since it is more convenient for embedding the code I am using. 
For my thesis, I am building a stock-flow consistent macroeconomic model. Among other things, this necessitates the inclusion of some rather large tables representing the balance sheet, transactions flow, and revaluation matrices of my model. I have written these in Latex and am now wondering whether there is any way to import these into a markdown. 

The largest of these tables is the following in Latex code:
\begin{landscape}
\setlength\tabcolsep{5pt}
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\tiny
\caption{Transactions flow Matrix}
\begin{tabular}{lccccccccc|c}
\hline \hline
&\textbf{Households}& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{Firms}}& \textbf{Bank 1}&\textbf{Bank 2}&\textbf{Bank 3}&\textbf{Financial Firms}&\textbf{Government}&\textbf{Central Bank}&$\Sigma$\\
&&Current&Capital&&&&&&&\\
\hline
Consumption&$-C$&$+C$&&&&&&&&0\\
Cap. Investment &&$+I$&$-I$&&&&&&&0\\
Inventory Acc. &&$+ULC*\Delta Inv$&$-ULC*\Delta Inv$&&&&&&&0\\
Depreciation K &&$-\delta_k*K$&$+\delta_k *K$&&&&&&&0\\
Gov. Spending &&$+G$&&&&&&$-G$&&0\\
Taxes &$-T$&&&&&&&$+T$&&0\\

CB profits&&&&&&&&$+PCB$&$-PCB$&0\\

Fees&&&&$+fee_{b1}$&$+fee_{b2}$&$+fee_{b3}$&$-fee$&&&0\\
Interest LL&&$-iLL$&&$+iLL_{b1}$&$+iLL_{b2}$ &$+iLL_{b3}$&&&&0\\

Interest Deposits&$+iD$&&&$-iD_{b1}$&$-iD_{b2}$&$-iD_{b3}$&&&&0\\
Int. Bank Bonds&&&&$-i_{BB}*BB_{b1, -1}$&$-i_{BB}*BB_{b2, -1}$&$-i_{BB}*BB_{b3, -1}$&$+i_{BB}*BB_{-1}$&&&0\\
Int. Gov. Bonds&&&&&&&$+i_{GB}*GB_{-1}$&$-i_{GB}*GB_{-1}$&&0\\
Int. Bills&&&&$+i_{Bill}*Bill_{b1, -1}$&$+i_{Bill}*Bill_{b2, -1}$&$+i_{Bill}*Bill_{b3, -1}$&&$-i_{Bill}*Bill_{ -1}$&$+i_{Bill}*Bill_{cb, -1}$&0\\
Net IB Int. &&&&$\pm iIB_1$&$\pm iIB_2$&$\pm iIB_3$&&&&0\\
Int. CB advances&&&&$-i_{cb}*A_{b1, -1}$&$-i_{cb}*A_{b2, -1}$&$-i_{cb}*A_{b3, -1}$&&&$+i_{cb}*A_{-1}$&0\\
Saving&$(Sav_h)$&$-Sav_f$&$+Sav_f$&$(Sav_{b1})$&$(Sav_{b2})$&$(Sav_{b3})$&$(Sav_{ff})$&$(Sav_{g})$&$(0)$&0\\
$\Delta$ Deposits&$-\Delta D$&&&$+\Delta D_{b1}$&$+\Delta D_{b2}$&$+\Delta D_{b3}$&&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Gov. Bonds&&&&&&&$-p_{gb}*\Delta gb$&$+p_{gb}*\Delta gb$&&0\\
$\Delta$ Bills&&&&$-\Delta Bill_{b1}$&$-\Delta Bill_{b2}$&$-\Delta Bill_{b3}$&&$+\Delta Bill$&$-\Delta Bill_{cb}$&0\\
$\Delta$ CB advances&&&&$+\Delta A_{b1}$&$+\Delta A_{b2}$&$+\Delta A_{b3}$&&&$-\Delta A$&0\\
$\Delta$ Interbank Lending&&&&$- \Delta IBL_{b1}$&$- \Delta IBL_{b2}$&$- \Delta IBL_{b3}$&&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Interbank Borrowing&&&&$+ \Delta IBA_{b1}$&$+ \Delta IBA_{b2}$&$+ \Delta IBA_{b3}$&&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Reserves&&&&$-\Delta R_{b1}$&$-\Delta R_{b2}$&$-\Delta R_{b3}$&&&$\Delta R$&0\\
$\Delta$ Mortgages&$+\Delta M$&&&$-\Delta M_{b1ns}$&$-\Delta M_{b2ns}$&$-\Delta M_{b3ns}$&$-\Delta M_s$&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Long Term Loans&&&$+\Delta LL$&$-\Delta LL_{b1}$&$-\Delta LL_{b2}$&$-\Delta LL_{b3}$&&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Short Term Loans&&&$+\Delta SL_f$&$-\Delta SL_{b1}$&$-\Delta SL_{b2}$&$-\Delta SL_{b3}$&$+\Delta SL_{ff}$&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Firms' equity &&&$+p_{ef}*\Delta e_f$&&&&$-p_{ef}*\Delta e_{f}$&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Bank Bonds &&&&$+p_{bb}*\Delta bb_{b1}$&$+p_{bb}*\Delta bb_{b2}$&$+p_{bb}*\Delta bb_{b3}$&$-p_{bb}*\Delta bb$&&&0\\
$\Delta$ Fund Shares &$-p_{eff}*\Delta e_{ff}$&&&&&&$+p_{eff}*\Delta e_{ff}$&&&0\\
\hline
$\Sigma$&0&0&0&0&0&0&0&0&0&\\
\hline
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\end{landscape}

As can also be seen from the attached file, the table thus produced is fairly complex and large. Is there some way to simply import this code into my rmd file, or some straightforward way to convert this into markdown? All the options for creating tables in markdown so far seem very cumbersome and do not seem to produce results which look as nice, or they are specifically designed to create tables from R objects which is not relevant for my purposes.
Any help would be appreciated.

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Re: Importing Latex tables
parts:
Consider two options: (1) produce html directly with the htmlTable package in R or (2) use HeVeA (http://hevea.inria.fr/) which does a nice job converting to html.
Frank

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Importing Latex tables
parts:
Yes and no. Technically rmarkdown passes anything it does not understand on to whatever comes after rmarkdown. If you have chosen to make pdf output then the next step is a LaTeX processor, and simply including it in the text of your document will work. On the other hand, if you produce html or docx, the LaTeX code will not make sense.

I happen to think using knitr WITHOUT rmarkdown (raw LaTeX with r blocks) is more straightforward if you want to build something as ambitious as a thesis... but other people have different opinions on this.
